name: Olfactory pathway
summary: Olfactory receptor neurons in the nasal epithelium send unmyelinated axons through the cribriform plate to synapse in the glomeruli of the olfactory bulb on mitral and tufted cells, whose axons form the olfactory tract. At the anterior perforated substance the tract divides: the lateral stria ends in the primary olfactory cortex of the uncus (piriform cortex), the amygdala and the entorhinal cortex, and the medial stria in the septal area and, through the anterior commissure, the opposite bulb. Smell is the only sense that reaches the cortex without a thalamic relay and one of the few that is largely ipsilateral, and its cortical stations in the medial temporal lobe explain olfactory auras in temporal lobe epilepsy.

origin.note: Bipolar olfactory receptor neurons in the olfactory epithelium (regenerate throughout life).

neuronChain.synapse: mitral and tufted cells in the glomeruli of the olfactory bulb
piriform cortex, amygdala, entorhinal cortex, olfactory tubercle (via the lateral olfactory stria); anterior olfactory nucleus and contralateral bulb (via the medial stria and anterior commissure)
orbitofrontal cortex via the mediodorsal thalamus (secondary olfactory cortex); hypothalamus

decussation.note: Mostly ipsilateral; some fibers cross to the opposite bulb.

waypoints.note: olfactory filaments through the cribriform plate
olfactory bulb and tract in the olfactory sulcus of the orbital surface
primary olfactory (piriform) cortex of the uncus via the lateral stria
relay to the orbitofrontal cortex for conscious odour identification

termination: Piriform cortex (uncus), amygdala, entorhinal cortex and, via the mediodorsal thalamus, the orbitofrontal cortex; hypothalamus for feeding and reproductive responses.

lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Anosmia or hyposmia, often bilateral; the commonest cause

lesionEffectsByLevel.level: Olfactory bulb or tract (meningioma, frontal tumor)
lesionEffectsByLevel.effects: Unilateral anosmia, often unnoticed, with frontal signs
Early hyposmia preceding motor or cognitive symptoms

pearls: Test smell in every patient with personality change: a subfrontal meningioma announces itself here
Olfactory hallucinations are almost always temporal lobe seizures, not psychiatric
